status: Checkpoint and aggregate projection admission implemented; streaming projection ownership remains open
projectionContract: TopKWithState and sortWithState admit result directories, records, fields and expression output in a separate projection scope. One ownership capture preserves source aliases until the checkpoint operation settles, including cancellation while a spill write is pending. This avoids repeated full-state captures per spilled run. A range loop replaces slice().map(); ordinary result ownership transfers to the caller at return.
Aggregate projection uses the per-row key scope. Group state copies retained scalar values; transient projection releases after group.add. Repeated rows do not accumulate projection workspace.

Projection enumerates own expression fields without Object.entries and writes own output properties, including special property names. Unscoped caller paths retain existing lifetime semantics; they are not claimed bounded by this change.

validation.fixtures: Existing expression HTTP/Worker fixtures now parameterize filters and projections. Three projection routes (aggregate, checkpoint top-k and checkpoint sort) run concurrently under 64/128 MiB shared pools and 2 MiB query caps. Actual serialized Parquet via HTTP 206/ignored-Range 200 and native local R2 verifies output parity, oversized expansion rejection and cleanup.
validation.cancellationAndSpecialFieldTests: Final focused set: 24 tests pass across projection and existing row top-k ownership. Deferred spill cancellation preserves at least the 4,000-byte projected payload until settlement, then releases to zero. Own special source fields remain data properties and frozen input is unchanged; unsafe explicit aliases retain existing validation rejection.

discoveredWriterBug.symptom: Direct equality on dictionary text 1 猫 returned zero rows despite matching decoded pages. All five groups were pruned; both generated extrema were dictionary text followed by a space, a 16-code-unit prefix.
discoveredWriterBug.cause: hyparquet-writer unconvertMinMax truncates both minima and maxima. A truncated maximum is not a safe upper bound.
discoveredWriterBug.fix: Pinned writer patch omits optional extrema beyond its bounded 16-code-unit representation, and surrogate-containing strings whose UTF-8 ordering is not proven by its JS comparator. Null counts remain. Non-null pages missing valid bounds disable the optional column index instead of emitting empty bounds. Offset indexes and short representable extrema remain.
discoveredWriterBug.tradeoff: Some string columns lose optional pruning metadata rather than incur unbounded statistic encoding or publish incorrect bounds. This is a correctness condition, not an unsafe opt-in mode.
discoveredWriterBug.coverage: Actual plain Parquet pages at 16/17 code units, longer shared prefixes and astral/BMP values; metadata assertions and equality result parity. A clean npm consumer repeats long-string equality after writing with the bundled patched writer.
discoveredWriterBug.distribution: Writer is bundled alongside the patched reader. Writer and Brotli licenses are included in third-party notices. Regenerated geo and Iceberg delete/manifest fixtures reflect corrected metadata.
discoveredWriterBug.limit: This writer change does not repair already-written files containing invalid bounds; historical metadata trust requires separate review.

remaining: Streaming ordinary/ordered projection needs batch-to-consumer ownership transfer; a query-long scope would retain every projected batch and is not the intended contract.
Borrowed reference-selection projection, DISTINCT keys, partition merging and remaining evaluator internals still require allocation integration.
Complete F1-F6/M1-M2/V1-V3 acceptance and refreshed coverage/reference gates remain open.
